articleTitle: An Efficient Analysis of EM Fields Into Shielded Enclosures Excited by ESD Through Rectangular Slots
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Coupling of e.m. fields due to electrostatic discharge exciting rectangular apertures in a rectangular cavity has been theoretically and experimentally investigated. In particular, the tangential electric field in the aperture has been evaluated by a rigorous approach that employs the equivalent principle leading to an integral equation, solved by the method of moments (M.O.M.). Then the theoretical voltage, induced in a square loop inside the cavity, has been compared with experimental voltage obtained in the same condition. Numerical simulation is in good agreement with experimental results up to 1 GHz.

articleTitle: Electric Fields Close to Triggered Lightning
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Simultaneous three-station electric field measurements at 30 m, 50 m, and 110 m from triggered lightning at Camp Blanding, Florida are reported. Characteristics of the recorded field waveforms due to leader-return stroke sequences lowering negative charge to ground are discussed.

articleTitle: Enhancements to Stirred Mode Chambers by the Use of Pseudo-Random Phase Reflection Gratings
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A method of increasing the mode density in a reverberant chamber in the critical low frequency region of operation is described. The technique relies on the use of pseudo-random phase reflection gratings on the walls of the chamber to produce diffuse reflections. Both experimental realisation and the TLM modelling of the chambers are described. The effect on both the mode density and the Q factors of the indiviual modes are investigated.

articleTitle: Computer Tools for the Analysis of Electromagnetic Compatibility in Switched Mode Power Supplies
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper part of a CAD tool to design Switched Mode Power Supplies (SMPS) taking into account electromagnetic interference (EMI) problems is described. In particular three problems related to EMC in SMPS are considered: parasitic interferences between tracks, radiated noise and conducted noise. The communication presents the results obtained up to now by our group, showing comparisons between simulation and measurements in several situations.

articleTitle: The Transient Field Distribution Near the Encapsulation of GIS
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents the evaluation of the transient field distribution near the encapsulation of a GIS-model. The discretization of the geometry has been performed with the help of a computer program which uses finite element method to calculate the transient field behaviour of the discretized GIS-model. The GIS-model used to perform these investigations has been constructed in a manner which minimizes internal reflection; this precaution was necessary to achieve a more precise knowledge concerning the transient behaviour of the bushing and to improve the method of detection. The simulation results were completed by making reference to the transient field distribution measurement in the modelled GIS. A field probe detects the transient electric field and transmits that information via a fiber optic link to a transient digitizer. The advantage of this method lies in the dielectric transmission from the probe to the transient digitizer. This measurement procedure reduces the distorting influence of the probe upon the electric fields. The measurement results are also presented within this paper.

articleTitle: Quality and Sites Correlation of Anechoic Chambers
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Reproducible results of automated radio interference field strength measurements can only be obtained in screened anechoic chambers. In order to enable a comparison between anechoic chambers and open area test sites, both types of test sites have to meet the same requirements. The proposal to introduce a specific chamber factor might aid in solving the problem of how to take larger deviations into account [1]

articleTitle: High Frequency Equivalent Models for Multiconductor Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Calculation procedures are developed to find models for close conductor lines (cables). The skin, proximity effects of conductors and lossy earth return are taken into account. A new approach has been developed with the aim of determining the values of equivalent model parameters of close conductors in a frequency range covering [ 0 Hz, 50 MHz ]. A good agreement between calculated results and those obtained experimentally is observed.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC) and Railway Systems
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Using electricity within Railway system is attractive both for community and railways company itself : Advantages as global economy, environmental protection, operational benefits as flexibility, reliability, must be mentioned : it is important for new lines specially in case of high speed. That leads to consider the consequences of existence and operating electrical works to allow EMC regarding neighbouring system and within railway system itself. European Community E.C.has published a lot of paper as EMC Directive (89/336), Public Procurement Directive (90/531) and Railway Development Directive (91/440); E.C. is preparing a new one dealing with High Speed Interoperability. Railways world - world means operators and manufacturers - has to bring answers to allow coming into force of the directives above mentioned : it is the sense of the work undertaken within CENELEC (EEC countries and EFfA Countries). So Railway people are present in Cenelec TC 110 (EMC Directive) and Cenelec TC9X (Electricity in railway transportation): final results will be EMC performance regarding a product (a convenor, a car, a locomotive, ... ) or constraints between the whole railway system and a neighbouring system or within the railway system between infrastructure and train. Mains facts of the work in course are : - update the existing results, for example CCITI Directives (1989 Edition), multiconductor model and associated limits - identify interfaces within railway or with neighbouring - identify railway environment characteristics by setting on measurement methods taking into account partly moving system and common test campaigns. Intermediate results will be : - the ability of preventing disturbances at the source by choosing adequate feeding schema (Booster Transformer, Autotransformer) or few disturbing locomotives - the inventory of the disturbances (sources and values) generated by the whole railway system or suffered by a rail way product Final results of all these works are necessary to enforce directives (for instance EMC one on 1st of January 1996) and to improve railway transportation in the respect of a general EMC approach.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Electromagnetic Diffusion of ESD Current in Non Perfectly Conducting Metallic Plates
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The problem of the electromagnetic diffusion of interfering currents due to electrostatic discharges occurring in metallic plates is modelled via a magnetic scalar formulation and a finite difference approach in the frequency domain. The algebraic equation system obtained is numerically solved by means of iterative over-relaxation techniques. The scalar potential formulation proposed allows to limit the discretization only to the conductor region, saving computational time. Finally it is shown how this modelling can be used to predict the ground over-voltages and the near field interferences caused by ESD currents.

articleTitle: GTEM Cell: A New Tool for EMC Measurements
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Consideration was given to the utility of GTEM cells in determining the electromagnetic compatibility of electronic devices. The GTEM cell made use of in our study was designed and constructed by the staff of the Institute of Telecommunication and Acoustics, Technical University of Wrocław. It was found to be useful not only in vulnerability tests of electronic devices exposed to pulse-type or continuous electromagnetic waves, but also in emission testing.

articleTitle: Calculation of Voltages and Currents on Lossy Multiconductor Transmission Line Systems in the Time Domain
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: If only quasi-transverse-electromagnetic waves exist and the transmission line system can be segmented into electrically short elements, the use of the transmission line theory is admitted. The calculation of interfering values of a multiconductor transmission line (MTL) system in the time domain as function of path and time can usually be performed only numerically. A method of characteristics according to MASSAU is introduced in this paper. This method of characteristics is suitable to calculate the voltages and currents on non-uniform lossy multiconductor transmission line systems with non-linear tennination elements and the influence of an external field.

articleTitle: Characterisation and Measurement Methods of Shielding Enclosures: A Practical Experience.
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The characterisation of shielding materials and enclosures is a rather complex measurement Since long time, measurement methods have been used based on the measurement of the surface resistance for the characterisation of materials and MIL STD 285 for the characterisation of enclosures. However, the last method requires large boxes and the method fails when applied to small boxes. In this paper, some valuable methods are discussed, even as an explanation of the failing mechanism of other ones.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Disturbances in Commutation Cells for Different Technologies of Silicon Components
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: High frequency behaviour of static converters depends on the silicon component technology, this paper shows how changes occur in the cell according to different technologies : MOSFET or IGBT switches and different diodes : snap-off or soft. This study is carried out using a theoretical analysis of a commutation cell with elementary models of the components. The behaviour of the cell is represented by plotting the EMC operating point on a reference taking interference energy and Joule losses into account, this allows us to conclude on the cell sensitivity as regards to the electrical parameters, according to the technology.

articleTitle: Modeling a One Class of the Non-Gaussian Processes Using Excited Non-Linear Filter
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A generating model of the nonGaussian narrow-band process, based on its interpretation as stationary output of a dynamic non-linear filter excited by the white Gaussian noise, is considered. The model may be effectively used in hard-ware or soft-ware simulators of quite differential phenomena from random attenuation of radio signal in both outdoor and in-house communication channels until charge oscillations in superionic conductors

articleTitle: The Time Domain Finite Element Method Applied to a Lightning Return Stroke Model
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A lightning return stroke channel is represented by a transmission line model with high losses. The point-matched TDFE method is used to solve the telegraph equations that represent the line dynamic behavior. The results show the strong effect of losses and comparisons with the EMTP (Electromagnetic Transients Program) are presented.

articleTitle: A New Broadband EMC Antenna for Emissions and Immunity
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A new broadband antenna is presented which is suitable for both EMC emissions and immunity testing over the 30 MHz to 1 GHz frequency range. The antenna was designed using a thin-wire integral equation based moment method package. The results of the modelling programme are compared with experiment and a comprehensive evaluation is made of the geometrical parameters which determine the performance of the antenna.

articleTitle: Prediction Model of Transient EM Field Due to Sliding Contact Arcing in Urban Rail Systems
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The sliding contact arcing in urban rail transit systems is a source of radiated electromagnetic interferences. A prediction model of the radiated electromagnetic field is proposed. The non-linear volt-ampere characteristic of the electric arc, its multiple restrikes and the mechanical rebounds of the trolley on the feeding line, are taken into account. The arc current is evaluated by the solution, in time domain, of a set of nonlinear ordinary differential equations by means of an hybrid Finite Differences scheme. The transient radiated fields, their frequency spectra and lateral profiles are evaluated according the International Standards.

articleTitle: EMC Training Needs in the Telecommunication Industry
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Due to the appearance of the European EMC directives as well as of severe EMC requirements of customers, the importance of EMC in the telecommunication industry is continuously growing. An important part in a systematic approach to handle EMC problems, is the education of the designers. An internal EMC course has been given to a large group of designers. From their comments a clear direction is shown: a strong need for EMC training, complemented with a practical design guide, all at the level of the designers.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Coupling by a Loaded Multiconductor Transmission Line Through an Aperture in an Infinite Metallic Screen in Presence of a Ground Plane
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The structure composed by a wire running above a ground plane and passing through an aperture in a semi-infinite metallic screen is analysed from an electromagnetic point of view. A very accurate low frequency solution is obtained by representing the field quantities in a suitable spectral domain and by treating the wire current as a filament current. A transmission line model of the structure, based on the scattering parameter representation, for both internal and external excitation is derived. Finally, the result is extended to the general case of a cable bundle.

articleTitle: Radiation Losses in the Time Domain Transmission Line Method
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The classical transmission line method only allows to take into account the propagation of a TEM mode, then all phenomena of radiation are neglected. As these phenomena become important when studying EMC coupling problems, an original formalism is proposed to introduce radiating losses in this method. Some example will validate the method and show the versatility of this approach.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Electronically Compensated Current Transformers Affected by Conducted and Radiated Interference
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper deals with the performance analysis of electronically compensated current transformers (ECCTs) in a noisy environment. To this end, an ECCT model is developed to evaluate the effects of conducted and radiated noise sources in different working conditions. The analysis highlights the noise sources most affecting ECCT performance and the design solutions for improving ECCT immunity.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Correct Computation of Electromagnetic Disturbance Propagation Through Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this work, the authors present an analysis for the relative significance of the transmission line impedance components, as a fundamental aspect for the correct evaluation of disturbance propagation through the line.

articleTitle: Analytical and Experimental Studies of EMC Problems in Cable Harnesses
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Analytical and experimental study of the performance of coaxial cables in different frequency ranges has been carried out. Various computer models have been developed to predict the effects due to the inductive and capacitive coupling in parallel cables under different circumstances. Of particular interest is the SPICE based model reported here which is capable of predicting the resonance effects. To validate the computer models developed, experimental results were obtained in a range of frequencies for several braided coaxial cables with varied parameters.

articleTitle: An Innovative EMI Reduction Design Technique in Power Converters
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The present paper deals with the problem of reducing Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) of switched-mode power converters using gate controlled devices such as IGBTs and Power MOSFETs. In order to reduce power losses these systems rely on fast-on/off time pulses, thus producing emissions due to the high-frequency spectral content of pulses. An original design method for switched-mode power supplies is developed allowing to obtain an acceptable compromise between power losses and EMI. Emphasis is placed on the analysis of a single switch voltage regulator in order to demonstrate that it is possible to control the emissions of the device by handling the parameters of the driver circuit. Theoretical analysis is discussed and compared with experimental results of the investigation on the spectrum amplitude of the emissions.

articleTitle: Critical Review of Standards on Human Exposure to Electromagnetic Fields
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Big differences in parameters of human exposure to electromagnetic fields, their temporal characteristics and reference values may be observed not only among the standards of different states and organizations, but also among the standards relating to different types of equipment and human activities. In the report the main attention is focused on the comparison of Russian standards on one hand and European and American ones on the other for controlled enviroment. Some examples of EM fields at workplaces of electroheat industrial equipment are given.

articleTitle: Multiconductor Transmission Leve Theory for Shielded Cables Under Consideration of the Environment
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Each line of a shielded multiconductor transmission line possesses its own transfer impedance and transfer admittance, whereby only the former is a characteristic of the cable. The problems occuring while measuring these quantities by using the standardized triaxial measurement set-up are discussed. A procedure based on a generalized multiconductor transmission line theory is presented which allows to handle the coupling parameters as normal per unit length parameters. The theoretical restrictions are pointed out.

articleTitle: International Standardization in the Field of Electromagnetic Compatibility
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper is structured as follows: 1. The International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) 2. CENELEC and the IEC/CENELEC cooperation agreement 3. Other international organizations for EMC standardization 4. The different kinds of EMC standards (IEC publication 1000) 5. The main electromagnetic disturbances 6. The different product categories 7. Legal or contractual status of EMC standards 8. Overview of IEC work on EMC standards 9. EMC standardization with regard to human safety

articleTitle: Calculation of Transient Pulse Propagation Through Non-Linear Magnetic Sheets with an Error-Based Approach
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper deals with a numerical formulation of Maxwell equations based on the edge elements and the minimization of the constitutive error. The formulation provides two dual solutions which can also be used to have an indication of the distribution of the numerical error in the solution domain. The method is applied to the calculation of transient pulse propagation through conducting nonlinear magnetic sheets. In this case, an iterative technique which is very efficient in matching the wave propagation in the vacuum to the magnetoquasistatic diffusion inside the conducting material is also proposed and applied.

articleTitle: An Innovative Bulk Current Injection Probe
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper deals with improvements in the field of susceptibility measurements with the Bulk Current Injection (BCI) method. An innovative probe for bulk current injection is described. The novelty of the probe consists of extended wideband capability, low volume and high efficiency.

articleTitle: A Non-Destructive Method for Measuring the Resistivity of Conductive Plastic Compounds
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper describes a new device developed for the measurement of the material electrical conductivity, known as the Faradex meter or eddy current R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf>-meter. This instrument determines the square resistance (R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf>) of a material by measuring the attenuation between two loop antennnas caused by induced eddy currents in the material of the sample between the antennas. This new eddy current R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>-meter is non-destructive and handy to use. It was specially developed to measure the square resistance of components moulded from stainless steel fibre filled plastic compounds. From a theoretical as well as from an experimental point of view, there is a good correlation between the results of four-point resistivity measurements and the results obtained with the eddy current R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>-meter. The square resistance can be used to calculate the shielding efficiency of the material for both near and far field conditions. There is also a good correlation between the far field shielding measurement and the shielding efficiency calculated from the eddy current R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>-meter results and between the near field magnetic shielding measurement (TEM-cell) and the shielding efficiency derived from the new resistivity measurement.

articleTitle: Influence of the Antenna Structure of Hand-Held Telephones on the EM-Field Exposure of the User
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A hand-held telephone held close to the head of a user is simulated by the finite integration and the integral equation techniques. The influence of the type and the mounting point of the antenna is investigated by a parametric: study. Guidelines for an antenna configuration with minimum EM-field exposure for the user are derived.

articleTitle: Radiated Emission from Railway Traction Line: A Numerical Prediction Model
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A prediction model of the radio frequency (RF) noise generated by a moving railway traction vehicle into the neighborhood of railway systems is presented. The frequency response of the traction railway line is evaluated by a numerical approach based on the method of moments in presence of sliding contact between pantograph and contact conductor. The wire grid model of the multiconductor transmission line (MTL), traction vehicle, pantograph and arc sliding contact is debated. The configuration of the high speed railway traction line that will be realized in Italy is examined in the applications.

articleTitle: A New Non Linear Model for Immunity Prediction of BJT Devices
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Aim of the paper is to define an equivalent circuit suitable to simulate the behavior of Bipolar Junction Transistors in presence of RF interferences. The circuit parameter values are all directly derived from the device technology. The model is validated by simulating the input stage of an Operational Amplifier and comparing the calculated offset voltage change due to the RF rectification with the experimental results. The agreement between experimental values and simulated ones seems very good.

articleTitle: A Numerical Procedure to Analyze Electromagnetic Excitation of Wire Structures Through an Aperture: Theoretical Considerations and Measurement Comparisons
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: An efficient numerical procedure for the analysis of electromagnetic field penetration through apertures of arbitrary shape in a perfectly conducting, infinite planar screen of negligible thickness has been recently presented. This technique allows to analyze cases in which the aperture is located in the neighbourhood of wire structures. These latter may be positioned on one side of the screen or on both sides. The same problem can be solved also in the presence of conducting wires penetrating the aperture. The numerical results obtained by the aforementioned technique are here compared with experimental data to check the accuracy of the numerical procedure.

articleTitle: Critical Examination of Susceptibility Test Methods
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The lack of definition in some susceptibility test methods on one side and the lack of experience on the other side make the choice of suitable test instrumentation difficult and prone to big errors. While the electromagnetic characteristics of radiating structures have been largely discussed in the literature no sufficient attention has been paid to the amplifiers which may represent the most critical part of the overall susceptibility tes t system because of the large amount of investment required and because of the expected quality of test results. This paper examines the definition of test limits paying attention to both the amplitude and the frequency spectrum of susceptibility signals especially when power amplifiers are operated near saturation.

articleTitle: Frequency Characteristics of Networks Measurements and Calculations
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: On this paper electromagnetic compatibility is evaluated from the point of view of frequency dependence of network impedance. This dependence is represented by a frequency characteristic determined by means of measurement and calculation procedures. Both these procedures are dealt with in this paper, and the methodology of frequency characteristic measurements in briefly presented. At the same time possibilities of calculation in more complicated networks using dominant transformer consumption method are investigated.

articleTitle: Limitation of Harmonic Pollution on MV Networks by Means of Proper Connection Criteria and Corrective Devices
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Harmonic pollution in some areas of MV distribution network of ENEL, Venice Area Board, have reached by 1991 critical values (THD(V)~15% at HV/MV substation busbars) especially in mountain areas, due to the relatively low short circuit power and to the presence of a large amount of six pulse AC/DC rectifiers (up to 60% of total required power of HV/MV substations) used at ropeway installations. As a consequence ENEL developed, on the basis of digital simulation, proper connection criteria for ASD equipped ropeway installations and planned, realized and tested some correction interventions for existing plants. These criteria, similar to the ones given in IEEE 519 STANDARDS, also assure the respect of CENELEC limits (EN 50160) on voltage harmonic pollution. The paper describes the connection criteria and reports the results of the different measurement campaigns, performed at 1991, 1992, 1993 and 1994 to check, both the effect of connection criteria and the real field behaviour of four different devices to reduce ASD current harmonic emissions, together with some indications about their cost.

articleTitle: Programmable Controllers Performance in Presence of Industrial Interferences
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) works near many noise sources which can have strong effects on their performance. The paper analizes the effects of conducted and radiated noises on hardware and logical structures of PLCs. Some suggestions to improve PLC performances and their interference immunity are be presented.

articleTitle: The UK's Regulations for Compliance with the EC Directive on Electromagnetic Compatibility (89/336/EEC) and Experience to Date
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: 1.1 There is a growing need to introduce EMC between a wide range of electrical and electronic devices which are used, increasingly, in everyday life and which by their very nature can act as radio transmitter or receiver, thereby causing serious interference with, for example, communication and electronic navigation systems. Furthermore, the use of mobile telephones and personal computers has grown dramatically over the past five years, as indeed have household electrical appliances incorporating microprocessor control circuits, all of which can either cause electromagnetic interference affecting the operation of other devices, or in themselves become affected by such interference thereby preventing them from operating as intended - sometimes with devastating results.

articleTitle: Environmental Considerations of Power Frequency Electric Field Egypt
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Environmental studies of EHV transmission lines are very important to provide a scientific basis for interpreting the kinds of impacts that are most apparent to persons who live, work or recreate near such lines. This work evaluates the electric fields in lateral profiles induced by the Egyptian 500 kV EHV lines. Also, the audible noise and radio interference emanating from these 1ines are presented. This work also evaluates the interaction between the electric field from EHV line and human for practical environment, namely desert, where the ground soil is largely dielectric for a certain depth. The current density at different sections in the the human body is computed for different sandy soil thickness and permittivity. The induced current along the human body, head to foot, is also presented. The short circuit current, when an isolated human touches a grounded rod is computed for different sandy soil thickness and permittivity.

articleTitle: Response of a Low Voltage Power Installation Network to the EM-Fields Generated by a Tem-Field Simulation Antenna and Natural Lightning EMP
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The response of a LVPI-network to transient EM fields generated by distant lightning, LEMP, is studied using a TEM-wave mode antenna. The analysis of the antenna geometry and the measuring system is presented in frequency domain. The antenna has a rhombic shape with three conductors separated at the central part The response of the LVPI-network to the TEM-wave generated by the antenna is compared with the EM response of the network to the EM-fields from natural lightning in the frequency range from 125 kHz to 10 MHz. We measured the CM and DM induced voltages and induced currents in some points of the object under test, OUT, in our case the installed LVPI-network. The analysis of the EM-response or the transfer function of the LVPI-network, caused by the simulated quasi-TEM mode fields and natural LEMP irradiation, is given and discussed in terms of the coupling mechanism. The performance of the LVPI-network under simulated and natural EM-field environment give us a better understanding of the susceptibility and the EMC conditions of these kind of systems.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Wave Interactions with Electric Propulsion Plasma Plumes
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The propagation of radio-waves in a non-homogeneous medium like the plasma generated by an electric thruster is being modelled using a new hybrid numerical scheme. This method combines a volume and a surface finite element resolution of MAXWELL equations.

articleTitle: A Multipurpose Software Package for Accurate Electromagnetic Analysis and Simulation of Arbitrary Shaped Waveguiding Structures
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A Finite Element software package for the quasi-static and dynamic analysis of general waveguiding structures is presented. The method can be applied to the electromagnetic analysis and circuital modelling of general inhomogeneous anisotropic lossy multiconductor transmission line and waveguiding structures. It also allows accurate characterization of shielding, proximity and coupling effects. In order to obtain solutions accurate to a pre-specifled degree a selfadaptive meshing technique is used. The quasi-static approach employs Lagrange elements and an electrostatic potential formulation. The dynamic analysis makes use of a spurious free formulation in terms of the electric or the magnetic field employing a non-standard element based on a combination of Lagrange and edge elements. Results are compared with previously published ones.

articleTitle: Numerical Method for the Calculation of the Shielding Effectiveness of Buildings
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A numerical method for the calculation of the shielding effectiveness of buildings that are constructed of reinforced concrete is presented. Applying the equivalence principle allows to replace the dielectric concrete by an equivalent polarisation current radiating in free space. This polarisation current as well as the electric line current along metallic wires are expanded into basis functions with unknown coefficients. These coefficients can be determined by constraining boundary conditions on metallic surfaces and within the dielectric volume, respectively. Once the currents are known, the electromagnetic fields at an arbitrary position inside and outside the building can be calculated. An example shows the flexibility of the method concerning the precise modelling of the geometrical shape.

articleTitle: Conducted Noise Affecting Signalling and Telecommunication Equipment in Underground Transportation Systems
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Electronic equipment, installed in railway or underground transportation systems, is a victim of electromagnetic interference, generated from power distribution system and carborne converters. As different environments exist, according to power system (AC or DC, different voltages...) and kind of traction converters (chopper or inverter actuated vehicles), it is difficult to define general norms and immunity limits. Nevertheless, the availability of guidelines, to develop equipment, suitable to be installed in a great variety of systems, is of a vital importance, in order to provide cost effective solutions for present and future needs of railway and local transit. In fact, this is also a target in view of the realisation of a unified European transportation network, and several CENELEC working groups are debating on this subject. It is, therefore, of a great usefulness to collect data about noise, that actually affects electronic devices in transportation systems: this paper refers to conducted noise that can be measured at power and I/O interfaces of electronic equipment installed in control rooms of a modern underground line.

articleTitle: Analysis of Overvoltages Induced in Buildings with Indirect Lightning Strokes
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Lightning overvoltages are created by direct strokes as well as in the way of induction phenomena. The last mentioned can be a severe problem for lightning protection of buildings equipped with computeres and other electronic devices. The attempts of induced overvoltages hazard evaluation which have been made up to present were considerably limited to deterministic approach. A new, different method is presented in the paper. This analysis affords possibilities to determine the number of strokes per year leading to dangerous overvoltages on the base of probabilistic approach.

articleTitle: Yield Loss and its Forecast of Semiconductor Devices Caused by the Particle Deposition on Silicon Wafer Forced by Electrostatics
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper describes the airborne particle transport and deposition on the silicon wafer caused by electrostatics in the clean rooms of semiconductor wafer fabrication The level of deposition density and velocity on silicon wafer surfaces forced by electrostatics have been reviewed\ and the effect of electrostatic charge on silicon wafer surfaces discussed.

articleTitle: CT2 (Cordless Telephone) Immunity Against Systems in Adjacent Bands
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Nowadays, the ability of a mobile system to operate within a heavy used spectrum is one of its major criterion of quality. In this respect, CT2/CAI standard, designed for being used in the 900 MHz band, had given some worrying. For this reason, measurements have been carried out on CT2 equipments in order to know their immunity against mobile and broadcasting systems operated, or intended to operate, in adjacent bands. The compatibility analysis on which these measurements were based provides an example of appropriate steps for spectrum engineering.

articleTitle: A Simplified Analytical Model of the Termination of a GTEM Cell
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The GTEM (GigaTEM) cell is proving a useful tool for studying objects under test in laboratory conditions [1] and, as such, is finding increasing utilization. Its advantage lies in allowing EMC measurements to be performed over a very wide band, up to a few GHz. This performance is achieved through a good match between the coax feed and the tapered cell, as well as an equally good termination, apt to simulate a wideband matched load. The present contribution provides a detailed but relatively simple model of the cell termination, including bulk resistors and absorbing cones, in the band 100-1000 MHz.

articleTitle: Estimation of Peak Return Stroke Currents from Measured Fields Without Prior Knowledge of the Return Stroke Velocity
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Eighteen subsequent return stroke electric fields from triggered lightning flashes were used to test the ability of a return stroke model introduced by Cooray [1] to predict the return stroke peak current from the measured fields without prior knowledge of the return stroke velocity. The results show that the original version of the model can predict the peak current with an error whose mean absolute value is about 13%. In this paper we introduced a physically reasonable modification to the model. With this modification, the model is capable of estimating the peak current with an error whose mean absolute value is about 8%.

articleTitle: Radiation Losses Representation in the Transmission Line Theory (TLT)
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A lot of publications deal with various types of transmission lines illuminated by electromagnetic fields. These fields cause additional currents and/or voltages on the line. Here the kind of the transmission line is not of interest. A shielded or unbraided cable can be considered. In contrast with this a lack of attention has been paid to the transmission line as a source of radiation. In this paper a procedure should be presented which allows the computation of line voltages and currents under consideration of losses due to radiation. The developed theory must be described as a second order theory because not merely the radiated fields caused by the transmission line current are computed but also the repercussion of these fields on the propagating current is taken into consideration by representing the losses as a created resistance per unit length. One can call this resistance the equivalent radiation resistance per unit length.

articleTitle: A CAD Method for the Extraction of EMC Relevant Geometric Parameters from Multilayer Layout
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A method based on the scan line algorithm for the extraction of EMC relevant geometric parameters from layout mask data is presented. The method is used to identify the critical interconnection nets, which contain critical discontinuities or critical couplings and allows the analysis of these nets by supplying SPICE sub-circuits representing interconnects. The method differs from other extraction methods in that (a) it does require a running time O(NlogN+l), where N is the number of input nets, l is the number of critical nets to be output; (b) it can be applied not only for chip layouts, but also for tape layouts, multi-chipmodul layouts and board layouts; (c) objects on a layout mask are not constrained to be rectangles, they may be arbitrary polygons.

articleTitle: Theoretical and Experimental Study of Power Lines with Regard to HEMP-Coupling and Radiation Effects
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The coupling of a HEMP to multiconductor lines is treated using an EMP-simulator for the experimental part, where structures consisting of different numbers of wires running in parallel are studied. Due to grounded wires and radiation at bents the induced currents and voltages are reduced. In a theoretical part the protective ratios for a power line are computed with an integral equation code.

articleTitle: Considerations on Penetration of Lightning Overvoltages Into Electronic Systems
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the paper it will be discussed different ways of overvoltages incoming into electronic systems within a structure due to direct and surrounding lightning strokes. These overvoltages may cause damages with partial probabilities which may be composed in order to obtain the complex probability of damage. These partial probabilities depend on several factors conditioned by construction feature, coupling conditions, screening effects. The frequency of damage of electronic systems is considered with reference to different location of surrounding strokes. The discussion is directed to the problems of assessment of the frequency of lightning overvoltages, their separate or cumulative treatment on the background of composition of partial probabilities of equipment damage due to single stroke.

articleTitle: How to Achieve Traceable, Repeatable and Compareable Data - from Worldwide Distributed EMC Test Laboratories
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Hewlett-Packard (HP) designs, manufactures and services electronic products and systems for measurement, computation and communications and operates over 20 EMC test laboratories worldwide. The basic business purpose is to create information products that accelerate the advancement of knowledge and improve the effectiveness of people and organizations. The company’s products and services are used in industry, business, engineering, science, medicine and education in approximately 110 countries. The company has worldwide about 97.000 employees, 20.000 of whom are employed in Europe. The net revenues 1993 were 20.317 Mio $, in Europe 7.177 Mio $. To stay successful in a very competitive market it is a must, to have forward-looking processes installed.

articleTitle: Lightning Overvoltages and Overcurrents on Telecommunication Subscriber Lines: Measurement Results in Italy
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Characterization of the electrical transient environment of telecommunication subscriber lines entails the measurements and analysis of lightning-related overvoltages and overcurrents. Programs for characterizing such activity in Italy have resulted in the recording of thousands of overvoltages and overcurrents at both ends of the subscriber line and, in some cases, along the line. For this study the measuring equipment was located in several and different locations. The paper presents the measuring equipment, location, environmental and cable characteristics and statistical evaluation of collected data!

articleTitle: Immunity of Cardiac Pacemakers and Risk Potential of Pacemaker Patients, with Special Regard to High-Power Medium-and Short-Wave Transmitters
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The susceptibility of pacemakers due to electromagnetic interference (EMI) and standards limit values will be analysed. In particular the situation for Swiss medium and short-wave transmitters is evaluated, including a typical mapping of the near-field situation around a short-wave antenna and an estimate of the possible risks for persons with a pacemaker. Although obligatory European standards for the derived limit values do not yet exist, the Swiss Telecom PTT has marked the high field areas around their medium and short-wave transmitters with a caution sign and also has attempted to inform the population. The limit value used by the Swiss Telecom PTT for this sign took into account actual electromagnetic field values, manufacturers' pacemaker data, standards limit values, as well as pragmatic considerations.

articleTitle: Models for The Analysis of the Electromagnetic Compatibility in Planar Microstrip Circuits
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Some models suited for the analysis of EMC problems in microstrip structures are presented and discussed. The models considered allow to evaluate both the disturbances induced by fields radiated from external sources and the emission from the structure itself. With regard to the induced disturbances, the responses for the cases of exposure in the far-field (uniform plane waves) and in the near-field (electric/magnetic dipoles) are analyzed.

articleTitle: Spice Analysis of Field Coupling to Multiconductor Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The SPICE implementation of the effects of electromagnetic interferences (EMI) on lossless multiconductor transmission lines (MTL) is presented. The field coupling model provides a set of equivalent lumped generators located at the ends of the transmission lines to account for the effects of the EMI, whose distribution in time and space is supposed to be arbitrary. The propagation of signals on MTLs is described in the SPICE implementation by means of the standard approach of the modal decomposition. The results show that the SPICE algorithm allows to efficently simulate the behaviour of an MTL with respect to interferences, both in time and frequency domain.

articleTitle: EMC Problems Associated with Power Factor Correction Capacitor Banks and Some Remedies to be Applied
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Two groups of problems associated with the application of power factor correction capacitor banks are presented and shortly analysed. The first one is the amplification of voltage distortion present in result of non-linear load supply, the second one are switching surges being the result of capacitor bank insertion into the circuit. The remedies based on capacitor banks modifications concerning their placement and rated reactive power are proposed to resolve the problems in view. A special algorithm of optimal control of LV capacitor bank switched in steps is also presented.

articleTitle: The Decoupling of DC Supply Lines
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Noise currents penetrating into the direct current (DC) supply lines and ground loops contribute largely to radiated emissions. Proper filtering of the DC supply lines to active circuits like oscillators, digital circuits, switchers etc. is necessary to block the noise currents. A good layout of the ground pattern on printed wiring boards (PWB’s) under the IC package can prevent the penetration of noise into ground loops. A wide-spread misbelief is that DC filtering can be achieved by connecting a capacitor between the supply- and ground pins of each IC. It is overlooked that the decoupling capacitors and the stray inductances of the supply- and ground tracks form resonant circuits, increasing the radiation. The application of ground planes and "power" planes is often insufficient to achieve compliance with mandatory radiation requirements. The only adequate solution lies in separate RC- or LC filtering of each individual active circuit. Reduction of emissions at board level implies lower demands on EMC measures at equipment level and will ultimately result in considerable cost savings.

articleTitle: Modelling for the Prediction of Interference Between Power and Signalling Currents in Railway Traction Systems
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Electrical circuit simulation models are described which enable a complete railway traction system, consisting of substations, traction drives, track signalling equipment, track and traction line to be assessed for low and audio frequency interference. Sample interference harmonic spectra are given for a 750 V DC traction system with inverter-fed traction drives and audio frequency track circuits. It is shown that the inclusion of a coupled line rail track/traction line model is vital to enable both common mode and differential mode effects to be studied.

articleTitle: Household ELF Environment Assessment
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents the work performed by some engineering units of a research project aimed to assess, on an epidemiological basis, possible influence on health of the exposure of human beings to extremely low frequency electric and magnetic fields. In order to estimate in a quantitative way the exposure to electric and magnetic fields an analysis of the household environment has to be performed. The purpose of the activity is to simulate the exposure dose of individuals from a reconstruction of their home environment by means of a questionnaire. To this aim the analysis of the emitting sources in the house and their relations with the people have to be performed. Afterwards, the contribution of all the emitting sources can be summed up obtaining a quantitative indication of the exposure field value to which the person is subject.

articleTitle: Rise Time of the Current Induced by a Lightning Discharge On An Overhead Cable
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Using the transmission line approach, the electric field radiated by a lightning stroke and its time derivative has been calculated for various positions of the receiving point and for various ground conductivities. The current induced on an overhead cable is determined, showing the relative influence of its horizontal part and of its vertical part during the first microseconds.

articleTitle: Impulse Responses for Crosstalk and Field Coupling Analysis of Lossy MTLs
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper, we discuss the evaluation and numerical representation of the time-domain characteristics of transmission lines. This is a major issue for any transmission line simulation method based on the solution of transient equations at the line ends. We show the structure and properties of the impulse responses corresponding to the line matched scattering parameters, and use such properties to draw general guidelines for the time-domain characterization of transmission lines. Both the convolution and the differential representation of the time characteristics are addressed, with the emphasis on their bandwidth. The influence of the line parameter models on the accuracy of the line time-domain characterisitics is discussed by numerical examples.

articleTitle: ELF Field Emissions from Electric Power Systems
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents the methods for calculation to 50 or 60 Hz electric and magnetic fields from power lines and substation. On the other hand, the technical basis limits of power frequency electric and magnetic field from power lines and substation are presented. These methods are comparison between theirs and with measurement values. These methods are applied to specific power line and substation.

articleTitle: Standardization Aspects and Legal Requirements in the Fields of Electromagnetic Compatibility and Radio Frequency Interference Suppression of Road Vehicles
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: To distinguish between the technical aspects of standardization and the compulsory legal requirements for the type approval of road vehicles this paper gives a survey of these different fields in terms of electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) and radio frequency interference (RFI) suppression.

articleTitle: EMC Modelling-the Test House Manger's View
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The views expressed in this paper are my personal opinions and not those of the IBM Corporation. IBM is a large company with many different types of operation co-existing within it. My department operates as a test house for both IBM and non-IBM customers, mainly working on product certification to European or International standards. This paper is written from the viewpoint of a test house manager, if we were a different type of EMC laboratory inside IBM, with a bias towards development work, then I may have a widely divergent view.

articleTitle: Computation of Capacitance Coefficients of Threedimensional Integrated Structures with The Boundary Element Method
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: With increasing clock rates and scale of integration in microelectronics and PCB-design problems of EMC achieve more and more importance [2],[7],[5],[1]. In the stage of development for an accurate simulation structures have to be considered which occur as transmission line discontinuities. Circuit models must be developed for such structures from the geometry and material properties in order to take into account these discontinuities. The embedding of such information into the design process reduces costs of redesign and gives access to prediction of malfunction in EMC sense. The objective of this paper is the computation of capacitance coefficients of threedimensional structures of arbitrary shape. In this case the indirect Boundary Element Method can be applied with advantage. The authors have developed a method to calculate capacitances values of transmission line discontinuities like connectors, vias etc. using the indirect Boundary Element Method.

articleTitle: Interconnect Modeling: Discontinuities and Spurious Effects
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Electromagnetic interference is omnipresent in all structureą where electromagnetic signals propagate, radiate and scatter. This obviously includes devices where, either due to packaging effects or the presence of circuit discontinuities, electromagnetic signals scatter and interact with the circuit housing and the enclosed circuit components. This presentation will focus on the problem of electromagnetic compatibility for microstrip lines in a closed or open geometry. A quantitative picture will be presented for the contribution to signal interference by fundamental effects such as radiation at circuit discontinuities and the generation of surface waves in substrate material layers. The minimization or optimization of coupling between lines, discontinuities and multi-level interconnects will be discussed and equivalent circuits will be presented.

articleTitle: Phenomena Affecting the Generation of Radio Frequency Noise in Railway Installations
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A railway is an extended installation from which noise at radio frequencies (in the range 9 kHz to 1 GHz ) is emitted into the neighbourhood. The sources of this noise are numerous and are interactive. This paper seeks to identify the sources, discusses their importance and attempts to give values for their contributions to the total emission. Among the sources are:—

articleTitle: Three-Dimensional Full-Wave Numerical Solution for the Crosstalk in Shielded Printed Circuit Boards
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: One of the problems that concern the EMC society is the crosstalk which is classified as an intra-system interference. In other words, the electronic system interferes with itself. This happens when conductors inside the system are close together such that the electromagnetic fields couple from one conductor to the other causing degradation of the system performance. Furthermore, the system shield may enhance the crosstalk for frequencies nearby the resonance of the shield itself. In order to accurately identify the crosstalk phenomenon, a recently developed hybrid numerical method [1] is employed in this paper to predict the crosstalk interference levels between signal tracks in shielded PCBs. Practically, most of the shield volume is empty except for the region occupied by the dielectric board and the attached signal tracks. This hybrid numerical method uses intelligently this fact to tremendously reduce the number of unknowns resulting from discretizing the problem volume for the numerical solution. Specifically, the empty region of the shield is modeled by a cavity with aperture. The solution of this cavity is expressed in terms of modal expansions with unknown amplitudes. On the other hand, the FEM is used to formulate the fields in the inhomogeneous part of the shield (the substrate and signal tracks). The two solutions are combined by virtue of the continuity conditions at the aperture of the cavity. In addition to the advantage of reducing the number of unknowns, the formulation described in this paper preserves the sparsity of the FEM matrix and does not require any matrix inversion. Also, the edge-based FEM is used with the expected advantages of not producing spurious modes and the ability of modeling sharp metal edges without the need to any singular trial functions [2]-[7].

articleTitle: A Simple Method to Predict Radiated Emission from Shielded Cables Exiting from a Physically Large Digital System
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A simple method to predict radiation from shielded cables exiting from racks of a digital system is given. The method is based on transmission line equations and the current along the cable is calculated for two cases: the line driven at one end and the line with distributed sources along the conductor. The radiated fields are predicted by Far Field approximations for the distance 3, 10, 30 m as required by CISPR 22 standard. Comparisons among analytic, numerical and experimental results are given.

articleTitle: Calculation and Analysis of Transient Electromagnetic Fields Under an EMP Simulator
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The aim of this numerical study is to check if an EMP simulator can be used with higher frequencies than usual ones. In this kind of problem. the spatial step for the structure discretization is imposed by the impulse rise time. Considering the fact that the dimensions of the structure are quite important, the computation is therefore impossible if a classical method is used (not enough memory available). To get round this difficulty, the idea is to combine two numerical methods (finite difference time domain method and integral equation method). In the following text, this combined method will be called the "mixed method". First, as confirmation of the validity and correctness of our method, we verified that the electric and magnetic fields computed near the generator with the FDTD Method are in close agreement with those obtained thanks to our "mixed method". Grounding our method on this validation, the electromagnetic field can be computed and discussed for the whole test volume. These results give us a lot of information on the effects of an increase in the frequency’ range on this kind of structure (previously built for lower frequencies)

articleTitle: A Nonlinear Distributed Parameter Model for the Transient Analysis of Surge Arresters in Power Lines
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The transient response of a high-voltage surge arrester pole is performed taking into account the propagation phenomena which occur when the geometrical dimensions of the structure become comparable to the wavelength of the exciting transient surge. The analysis is carried out considering an equivalent circuit with nonlinear distributed parameters. The terminal voltage and current are computed by solving the proposed simulation model consisting in a nonlinear integral equation system in the time-domain. The developed numerical solution algorithm is based on the recursive formulation of the integral equations and realizes a space-diagonal step-by-step procedure. The proposed model is applied to the analysis of the transient response of a ZnO arrester; comparisons with equivalent lumped parameter models are carried out.

articleTitle: The Cylindrical Shield in Transverse Non-Stationary Magnetic Field
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The aim of the paper is to analyze the shielding effectiveness and the different attenuation suffered by the electric, respectively magnetic components of the field in the case of an infinitely-long cylindrical shield in transverse non-stationary magnetic field (HF). The non-uniformity of the field outside and inside the shield is analyzed. The relations for shielding effectiveness are complicated, and in this context numerical analysis and pertinent graphics can help in order to understand better the behavior of this shield.

articleTitle: Modeling of High Speed Circuits in a Multilayered Environment
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Last year, a project was started at the Katholieke Universiteit Leuven to model high speed circuits in a multilayered environment. The approach used is based on the experience acquired during the last 10 years at the K.U. Leuven on the modeling of complex microstrip antenna structures. The reason to start with this project was the need to include a rigorous description of the high speed circuits feeding an antenna. It is evident that, with slight modifications only, it will be possible to use the extended model for EMC-purposes because radiation of the structures is included. In this paper, an overview will be given of the general circuit that will be modeled and of the general line of reasoning followed to model it. The results up to now will be discussed.

articleTitle: Response Characteristic of a Low Voltage Power Installation Network to the EMP Irradiation Obtained by an Impulse Current Injection Method
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper, a theoretical and experimental analysis of LEMP interaction with a low voltage power installation, LVPI, network is presented. The analysis was carried out using the current impulse injection method, which simulates transient conduction and radiation in LVPI networks caused by LEMP interaction. The validity of the approximation of CM current injection to simulate the interaction of LEMP with an individual LVPI network was particularly evaluated. Both single-earthing and multi-earthing of LVPI networks behave in different ways for LEMP interaction. Recommendations are given on the testing of the transient protection of LVPI networks regarding the non-linear effects caused by LEMP interaction.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation of Penetration and Coupling Using the TLM Method
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper describes progress in the modelling of penetration and coupling in configurations relevant to EMC. The application of the TLM method in modelling efficiently thin finite- conductivity panels and thin wires is outlined. Comparisons with experimental and theoretical results show that inexpensive numerical models are accurate enough for EMC studies and hence that whole system modelling is becoming feasible.

articleTitle: EMC Training Needs in Industry: Visualizing Electromagnetic Phenomena
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Altough designers of electronic equipment are perfectly aware of the laws of Maxwell, Ampere, Faraday. Coloumb, Kirchhoff, etc. they lack sufficient insight in the effects these laws have on their designs. In general, today's electronic engineers tend to overlook the electromagnetic phenomena involved in the processing of audio, video, data or other signals.
