Unwanted signals from an interference source reach a susceptible circuit, the parasitics of components and wiring providing the coupling path between both; the results are conducted and radiated emission and susceptibility problems. A basic problem in electronics is the invisibility of currents, voltages and fields. Clearly, it is easy for technical people to judge weaknesses in a mechanical construction, because they see them with their own eyes. Consequently, when the electrical phenomena are made visible to engineers, they will get a better understanding of EMC, without having to be EMC specialists. Years of EMC training, education and problem solving have led to the construction of simple tools, jigs, print layouts and other accessories that are used to demonstrate the invisible phenomena behind the processing of desired signals. Once understood, deviations from the expected are no longer black magic. The following is a summary of some important demonstrations and the necessary equipment

articleTitle: Novel Optoelectronic Electromagnetic Field Sensors
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: We present materials data, computer simulation and experimental aspects towards the development of electro-optic and magneto-optic sensors based on the Pockel's and Faraday effects, respectively. These passive, all-dielectric sensors will use semiconductor crystals, laser diode and fibre optic technology to measure electromagnetic fields at frequencies up to 2GHz.

articleTitle: Dual-Mode Filters for EMI Environment Improvement Related to Microvave Transceiver Equipment
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The design of wideband high selectivity dual-mode filter is considered. The analysis and synthesis techniques are based on the combination of two-and four ports approach. The recommendations of optimal resonators configuration are given to achieve maximum unloaded Q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> and favorable distribution the principal and higher oscillations modes. As an example, the frequency response characteristics of the 14-units bandpass filter operating at 8 GHz are presented. The insertion loss is 0.2 dB and bandwidth is 500 MHz.

articleTitle: Numerical Validation of an Improved Lightning Return-Stroke Modelling
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A numerical technique for correlating ground level return-stroke currents to the electromagnetic field at earth surface is proposed. The analysis has been made assuming a vertical lightning channel with a cross-section exponentially contracted from ground to cloud. The validity of the calculations has been confirmed by experimental observations available at several ranges. The main goal of these computations is to validate, in the region where the experimental results are absents, the analytical approach proposed by the same authors.

articleTitle: Field Distribution and Loss Due to Eddy Currents in Cylindrical Models of the Human Body
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The accurate estimation of the electric and magnetic fields inside the human body is of extreme importance, especially for the M.R.I. conditions. A method based on the numerical method of moments is presented, for determining the electric field and the eddy current density induced by a non uniform electromagnetic field in a cylindrical shell. A method based on the diffusion differential equation for the magnetic vector potential is used for the validation of the results. The high frequency alternating magnetic field is produced by a saddle coil configuration or by several co-axial circular current loops. Numerical results are given for frequencies up to 60 MHz. A comparison of the two methods shows that they produce similar results which deviate greatly from the often used, quasi-static solutions.

articleTitle: Highly Accurate Absorbing Boundary Conditions in Finite Difference Time Domain Applications for EMC Simulations
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this work, a special adaptation of Liao’s Absorbing Boundary Condition (ABC) is presented to optimize the solution for a class of EMI/EMC problems when using the Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD) method. The Liao ABC is constructed on a per-cell basis to accommodate the most likely direction of incidence on the mesh-terminating boundary. Numerical results are presented to demonstrate the validity of the formulation and the improvements it provides over traditional ABC applications.

articleTitle: Effective Penetration Depth in Spatially Periodic Grids: A Novel Approach to Homogenization
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Spatially periodic grids may shield effectively against radiation of some wavelengths. The theory of skin-effect well accounts for this, once an "equivalent homogeneous material" has been defined. We show how to perform this homogenization, by way of a computation at the level of the basic repetitive module, or (Bravais-) "cell" of the structure. The result is frequency dependent.

articleTitle: Overhead Transmission Lines Coupling Phenomena
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the energy transport and distribution networks, the high voltage overhead lines cross lines with inferior voltages, or they are in the close proximity of them. The coupling phenomena will appear in transmission lines ( overhead and underground), which may be induced in consumers equipment. The paper presents some aspects concerning the electromagnetic coupling of overhead lines ( 750 kV and 400 kV) with medium voltage electric lines, by studying: cables surface potential gradient increasing, transmission of polluting signals produced by high and ultra high frequencies. There is also analysed the influence of electrical and geometrical parameters on coupling phenomena ( line length, crossing angle, frequency signals, ground ). The study has been developed analytical, as well as experimental, by the aid of the experimental overhead line ( 110 kV - 750 kV, scale 1:1) of the High Voltage Laboratory of Power Systems Faculty - Bucharest "POLITEHNICA" University. There have been already obtained data results, using equipment type CISPR.

articleTitle: Application of NURBS Surfaces to the Analysis of Coupling Between Antennas on Board of Complex Structures
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A code called GONURBS, to analyze antennas on board of complex bodies is presented. The Geometrical Optics (GO) and Uniform Theory of Diffraction (UTD) have been used to analyze the effect of the structure in the radiation pattern of the antennas. The bodies are geometrically modelled by using NURBS (Non Uniform Rational B-Spline) surfaces. In addition to be accurate and efficient, the code is compatible with most of the modem CAGD (Computer Aided Geometric Design) available programs.

articleTitle: Lightning Induced Voltage on Distribution Lines with Shield Wires
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The work presents a program for lightning induced voltage calculations based on the theory proposed by S. Rusck. The methodology consists of applying an analytical expression originaly deduced for an infinite homegeneous line plus the necessary correction terms that take into account real line characteristics. Correction terms are modeled as sources of a transient calculation program that are injected in specific points of the line and the induced voltage can be obtained. The program determines induced voltages on two-conductor aerial lines consisting of grounded neutral conductors, shield wires, surge protectors, etc. Comparisons between this and other methodologies are presented. A group of digital simulation results is also presented to ilustrate how the program can be used to evaluate lightning performance of distribution lines.

articleTitle: A Gas Arrester Spice Model Considering the Voltage/Time Characteristics
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: For the development of nonlinear protective circuits the widespread circuit simulation software SPICE [1] is a useful tool if the necessary component models are available. An important component in these circuits is a gas arrester. SPICE can have severe numerical problems with such extreme nonlinear elements. A solution of this problem, a stable time-domain (and frequency-domain) SPICE-model of a spark gap is presented. An extension considering the dependence of breakdown voltage on the pulse steepness [2] is also presented.

articleTitle: EMC Performance Comparison of Shielded and Unshielded Data Transmission Systems
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: EMC emissions and immunity tests were performed on several shielded and unshielded twisted pair cabling systems for data transmission. Results are presented that show a properly designed unshielded system can equal or exceed the performance of shielded systems. Surprisingly, all of the shielded systems tested had immunity problems that were not present at any level of stress achievable by the test equipment for the unshielded system tested.

articleTitle: Human Exposure to EMFs: A New Moment-Method-Based Method
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A new version of the moment method is proposed, which takes into account possible a priori information on the structures of the model under test. This allows a reduction in the computational resources required to determine the electromagnetic field distributions inside dielectric bodies that differ partially from one another.

articleTitle: A Combined CAD Package to Predict and Minimise EM Radiation from a PCB at Design Stage
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A rationalised approach is introduced in this paper to. predict and minimise EM radiation from a printed circuit board (PCB) using a combined computer aided design (CAD) package. This CAD package has been developed by combining an electromagnetic (EM) computation tool, such as numerical electromagnetic code (NĘC)-2, with other circuit design packages (CDPs). The use of NEC-2 for this type of application has been, validated experimentally and theoretically. Both methods of evaluation are described in this paper and results showing good agreement are presented.

articleTitle: An Engineering Methodology for Electromagnetic Compatibility Control on Complex Systems
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Nowadays, the increasing size and the high integration rate of space systems make the control of the electromagnetic compatibility more and more difficult. New engineering tools are then required in order to anticipate and overcome potential EMC problems, as early as possible in the design phase. To match this ambitious goal, the TDAS-EMC (Test Data Analysis System for EMC) engineering framework has been developed by MATRA MARCONI SPACE for the European Space Agency (ESA-ESTEC). TDAS-EMC is articulated around a database management system, which enables engineers to classify EMC test data, specification and simulation results. Advanced prediction tools are embedded into TDAS-EMC to tackle EMC aspects on complex systems, for both conducted and radiated coupling modes. After a brief introduction, TDAS-EMC is described through its applications made on space systems.

articleTitle: The Transfer Impedance of Metallic Cable Trays
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility

authors.preferredName: M. J. A. M. van Helvoort
P. C. T. van der Laan

abstract: Cable trays can play a highly useful EMC role, because they can be designed to keep interfering voltages on wires and cables in the tray low. The transfer impedance is then of great interest and has been studied both theoretically and experimentally. For non-ferromagnetic trays with a different geometry and conductivity, the magnetic field at the middle line above the bottom of a tray can be represented by a single curve as function of frequency. The same applies to the current density at low frequencies. At high frequencies it can be calculated from the magnetic field.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Absorption in the Human Head for Mobile Telephones at 835 and 1900 MHz
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Computational and experimental techniques have been used to obtain specific absorption rates or SARs for the human head and neck for a number of typical mobile telephones, including some that are planned for the PCS frequency of 1900 MHz. The FDTD method is used for computations for a high-resolution MRI-based model of the human body with cell sizes on the order of 2 × 2 × 3 mm. For experimental measurements a head-shaped model made of tissue-equivalent materials simulating complex permittivities of skull, brain, muscle, eyes, and ears is used. The SAR distributions are critically dependent on the nature of the antenna and its placement vis à vis the handset and the human body. For many of the mobile telephones the peak SARs for any 1 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> of tissue are smaller than 1.6 W/kg considered acceptable by the ANSI/IEEE Safety Guidelines.

articleTitle: Treatment of Arbitrary Nonlinarely Loaded Thin-Wire Structures by Means of the Method of Moments
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A combined frequency and time domain procedure for the analysis of arbitrary nonlinearly loaded thin-wire structures will be presented. The computation of the frequency-domain data is based on the method of moments allowing an easy consideration of lightning phenomena and skin effect. Due to the modelling of the structures by thin wires the procedure is suitable for a large variety of EMC problems and configurations respectively. The subsequent analysis in the time domain with the additional nonlinear loads is performed by means of a time-marching procedure suggested in [1].

articleTitle: Correlations Between EMC Tests in Frequency and Time Domain
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: There are two basic measuring principles to test the electromagnetic compatibility of electronic systems against radiated electromagnetic fields. The measurement in time domain tests the EUT by a single field pulse with a small rise time. Measurements in frequency domain stress the EUT with a sinusoidal field at a discrete frequency. One disadvantage of the measurement in frequency domain is the time consuming test procedure which is necessary to scan the whole frequency range. Therefore it is investigated whether there is a correlation between measurements in frequency and time domain and how information from time domain measurements can be used for a frequency domain test following the time domain test.

articleTitle: Various Frequency Dependent Effects on Electromagnetic Fields (10kHz-1GHz) in the Vicinity of Automobiles
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Modern cars contain extensive electronic equipment and devices which operate at comparatively low levels. This equipment is endangered by electromagnetic radiation of transmitters. Of special interest is the influence of parasitic radiators represented by metallic structures, e.g. steel bridges and buildings as well as railings, in the vicinity of common streets on electromagnetic fields radiated by transmitters. Extensive measurements have been carried out in the frequency range between 23.4kHz up to 756MHz whereby particularly the shielding effectiveness of car-bodies has been investigated.

articleTitle: Surface Impedance Modeling of Debye-Media
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: For studying the interactions between a structure situated above a ground and an incident electromagnetic wave, a surface impedance formalism has been developed. This approach has already been developed for taking into account interfaces between vacuum and as soil of characteristics (ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>,σ) with ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Γ</inf> constant value. In this paper we propose to extend such a formalism to take into account interfaces between vacuum and dispersive media characterized by ε(ω) where permittivity follows a DEBYE's law. The validation of this formalism is made on various examples.

articleTitle: Magnetic Field Shielding Effectiveness Measurement Using a Quarter Loop Antenna
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The development of a new EMC antenna, namely the Q-loop antenna (a quarter of a loop antenna in front of 90° comer reflector) is described. Test device incorporating this newly developed antenna for measuring Shielding Effectiveness (SE) of conductive composite materials against low impedance wave are introduced and the test results are analyzed. A theoretical model of the Q-loop antenna is developed using image theory and the theory of pattern multiplication. Other parameters of this antenna are also derived analytically.

articleTitle: Conductive Coupling to Underground Cables of Infinite and Finite Length
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper addresses conductive coupling of an electrode to underground cables on the basis of an equivalent transmission line model [1]. Earth conduction effect and the condition for both infinite and finite length are considered in calculation of the voltage between sheath and core conductor, and current in core conductor, of the cables. Computational results are given and discussed.

articleTitle: Spatial Fields in Integrated Microstrip Structures
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Sommerfeld-type integrals are frequently encountered, when the fields radiated by current elements, embedded in lossless or lossy grounded slabs, have to be derived. These infinite integrals are, in general, difficult to evaluate numerically due to their highly oscillatory nature. In EMC, one has, often, to compute the Sommerfeld-type integrals many times in order to solve the integral equation for the unknown induced antenna current. Moreover, the computation must be repeated for a large number of frequencies in the process of constructing the transient response of the antenna. Therefore, it is evident the need for an accurate and efficient method for evaluating these type of integrals. In this paper we solve the numerical problem of evaluating the Sommerfeld-type integrals and show some computed examples related to a strip array antenna under an external TE excitation condition.

articleTitle: Crosstalk Simulation of Traces in a Multi-Layer Circuit Board
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The increasing of computer clock rates and the more stringent requirements in electronic packaging tend to decrease the performance of electronic circuits. Electromagnetic simulation by finite element method helps to solidify the design process when crosstalk reduces the capabilities of high performance circuit board. The device presented in this paper is a multi-layer circuit board which consists of seven signal traces plus one power plane and one ground plane. The objective of this simulation is to quantify induced voltages on quiet traces with one active trace in the device. All computations are made using the three-dimensional finite element software MSC/EMAS™.

articleTitle: Investigations on Suppression of Higher Order Mode Resonances in TEM Cells Using a Planar Terminator
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Excitation and suppression of higher order modes in TEM cells are investigated due to a variation of the applied terminator. Higher order mode excitation is caused by wave front deviating from TEM mode due to the spherical wave excited in the tapered transition. Distortions are measured in time domain by means of a fast probe system. A new computational method is introduced to determine excitable higher order modes and belonging resonant frequencies for conventional TEM cells. Results of a physically motivated model for TEM cells are in accordance with measurements concerning both TEM mode and higher order modes. The new construction principle of a planar terminated TEM cell yields markable resonance suppression. Measurements of a TEM cell equipped with a planar terminator correspond to simulation results of the introduced TEM cell model. Upper limiting frequency of this TEM cell design determined only by planar terminator radiation is increased by applying new developed modifications.

articleTitle: Anechoic Chamber Fitted with Ferrite Grid or Ferrite Multi-Layer Electromagnetic Wave Absorbers
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The characteristics of novel electromagnetic wave absorbers, such as a ferrite grid and a multi-layered structure with a rubber ferrite, are presented together with those of RF anechoic chambers line with these absorbers. The superior reflection attenuating characteristics are verified by experimental studies as well as calculations.

articleTitle: On MHD-Waves and Geomagnetic Pulsations in the Earth-Bound Space
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The solar flares, cosmic explosions or gamma-flashes of extraterrestrial origin are accompanied with generation of magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) disturbances in the Earth-bound space, We Consider the non-stationary processes connected with MHD-wave traveling over Earth’s magnetosphere and ionosphere. For the cold magnetosphere plasma it is shown within limits of linear theory that the frequency dependence of dialectric tensor <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\hat{\varepsilon}$</tex> (ω) assures the Alfven-magnetosonic waves interaction. Taking into account terms of order ω<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/ω<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> in decomposition <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\hat{\varepsilon}$</tex> (ω), where ω — frequency of wave, ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf>— gyrofrequency of ions, we receive the continuous generation One wave sort by another ( Alfven by magnetosonic wave and vice versa). Away from source the both waves travel over non-dissipative medium without any decrement at a small angles to magnetic field. This result is nontrivial, as far as usual magnetosonic wave is isotropic, and its amplitude decreases in inverse proportion to distance r from source. We have investigated the interaction of MHD-wave with high conductive gyrotropic layers (Hall conductivity σ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> appreciably exceeds Pedersen conductivity σ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>) of natural, or artificial origin. The diffusion processes of electric currents, induced by magnetofonie wave in gyrotropic layers are considered in quasi-stationary approximation. It is shown, that frequency and temporary characteristics of geomagnetic pulses generated by the currents in magnetosphere and on Earth’s' surface depend on the ionosphere parameters (gyrotropic layer thickness, Hall and Cowling Conductivities) and magnetic inclination. These results permit us to hope on opportunity of use frequency-temporary characteristics of pulses for lower ionosphere condition diagnostics.

articleTitle: Method to Define a Safety Zone for Mobile Earth Station! with Regard to Exposure to Electromagnetic Field
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper describes a study conducted to determine whereas safety precautions with regard to exposure to electromagnetic fields were needed for the earth stations in use in the satellite communication centres. The results are that for the fixed earth stations, their maximum level in the main beam is below the occupational exposure limit; but, for mobile earth stations, this limit can be exceeded close to the antenna and it's necessary to define a safety zone both in terms of occupational and general public exposure. A method combining theoretical calculations and measurements is proposed to define this safety zone.

articleTitle: Pulse Degradation of MO-Arresters
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Limiting overvoltages to non-critical values is the duty of MO-arresters. The extremely nonlinear characteristic of MO-material allows protection devices without spark gap. For voltages up to the operating voltage MO-arresters are highly resistive. For voltages higher than their rated voltage they limit voltage to a nearly constant value even with significantly increasing pulse current-peak. Although MO-arresters are made for carrying high currents the tests demanded do not check the long-term stability of arresters stressed with pulse-currents. 1EC 99-4 as well as ANSI/IEEE 62.11 only demand a test proving stability for 1000 h at raised a.c.-voltage and a temperature of 115°C. The experiments described show that pulse-degradation of varistors can occur and has to be tested properly. Pulse-degradation means that the characteristics of the MO-material are changed by pulse-currents applied to a varistor.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation of ULF Noise Electric Environment
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The results of investigation of atmospheric electric field pulsations in the frequency range from 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup> to 1 Hz are presented. The measurements have been performed at a height 1.5 m above the ground under fair weather conditions. For the analysis of pulsation characteristics the concept of a structural function D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">E</inf>(r) has been used. The found structural functions and temporal spectra of electric field pulsations allow us to single out an external turbulent scale L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> ≃ 20 ÷ 60m, characterizing the height of the surface layer. On the other hand, our results testify to the existence of electric field perturbations with the scales τ ≳ L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> = 60 m, which are caused, probably, by convective cells. One can note that a volume charge, formed due to the electrode effect, could be transferred by these cells along the Earth’s surface and carried off from it.

articleTitle: A Finite Element Method for Calculating Electromagnetic Fields Radiated by an Antenna
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The antenna theory with thin wire approximation is usually used to calculate electromagnetic fields radiated by a cylindrical conductor, either in the air or underground, whose radius is very small compared with its length. This paper presents a new approach which enables the same application to be processed by solving various formulations with the Finite Element Method (FEM). Currents in thin cylindrical conductors are taken into account without volume meshing. Fields radiated by leakage currents and by induced currents in ground, in the case of a buried conductor, are also taken into account. Simple examples which have already been discussed in literature are presented anil allow the different advantages of the proposed new concept to be highlighted.

articleTitle: Observations on the Adequacy of Transmission Line Coupling Models for Long Overhead Cables
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper reviews a technique for determining the response of a transmission line (TL) excited by an incident electromagnetic (EM) field. The Telegrapher’s equations are introduced first and a method of solution related to an EM scattering analysis is presented. It is shown that it is important to be consistent in treating the excitation sources on the line. Either the general high-frequency representations of the sources, or the low-frequency approximations may be used, but not a mixture of the two. A comparison of the TL solution with that provided by an integral equation for the same line geometry is then presented. It is apparent that for the particular example chosen for this paper, the TL model fails to provide an accurate solution. As a result, modifications first suggested by Prof. Degaque for treating the ends (or “risers”) of the line as additional transmission lines connected to the main line have been included in the coupling model. This provides results that agree very well with the integral equation solution.

articleTitle: A Moment Method Analysis of Radiation and Coupling Problems Using Basis Functions Defined Over Parametric Surfaces
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Geometrical modelling by NURBS (non Uniform Rational B-Splines) surfaces is combined with the Method of Moments in order to analyze radiation and coupling problems between wire antennas mounted over conducting surfaces. A special kind of subdomain has been introduced to represent the current around the points where an antenna connects to the surface. The approach has been validated considering radiation patterns of a monopole antenna on a conducting flat plane and mounted on a conducting cylinder. The results are compared with measurements or other methods. Good agreement is obtained in all cases.

articleTitle: A Time-Domain Iterative Approach to Correct the Transmission Line Approximation for Lines of Finite Length
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: We present an iterative approach to correct the results obtained using the TL approximation for lines of finite length above a perfectly conducting ground. The method can be applied both in the frequency- and in the time-domain. The proposed iterative procedure converges rapidly to the exact analytical solution for the case of an infinite line, and to the NEC solution for a line of finite length. Moreover, with only one iteration, an excellent approximation to the exact solution can be obtained.

articleTitle: Effects of Conducted Interferences on Microprocessor Based Measurement and Control Apparatus
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper deals with the effect of conducted interferences on a microprocessor-based measurement and control apparatus devoted to the differential protection of low voltage lines in electric energy distribution. This digital protection, based on the use of a Digital Signal Processor, and the conducted interferences, typical of the environment in which the apparatus is installed, are briefly described at first. The performance of a prototype in presence of these interferences is then analyzed in detail. The apparatus proves to be very reliable showing insensitivity to common mode and a high rejection to most of the considered differential mode interferences. A comparison with a traditional protection under the same interferences is finally reported.

articleTitle: A Procedure for Numerical Solution of Field-Excited Nonuniform Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The point-matched finite element-time domain method (FE-TD) is applied to study the susceptibility of nonuniform thin wires excited by a transient, nonuniform electromagnetic field. The scattered voltage formulation of transmission line equations is adopted and distributed voltage sources are considered. Field equations and transmission line equations are simultaneously solved at discrete time steps adopting the leap-frog scheme.

articleTitle: Influence of the Modulation Characteristics of an Interferer on the Performances of a 2 GHz Radio Relay - Protection Ratios -
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The increasing development of radiocommunication systems requires more and more compatibility studies to ensure the optimal use of the frequency spectrum. But the characteristics of these radiocommunication systems become more and more complex, each of them having their own particularities : analogue or digital devices using different modulation and specific technic access (TDMA, CDMA, FDMA...). The aim of this study is to compare the effect of the nature of one interferer (with different modulations and technics access) on the performances of a digital Radio Relay in the 2 GHz band.

articleTitle: Radiated Susceptibility Test. Accuracy and Traceability of the Measurement by Electric Field Sensors
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the paper a method for the performance assessment of an Electric Field Sensor and the calculation of uncertainty and confidence associated with it is described. The method is based on the exposure of the Electric Field Sensor under test to a known Electric Field. The influence of all the uncertainties of the measuring system is taken into account and the obtained result is considered as the uncertainty of the Electric Field Sensor Correction Factor. In addition, an example is given about the influence of the uncertainty of the Electric Field Sensor on the reliability of Radiated Immunity Tests.

articleTitle: A Quasi-Analytical Approach for the Analysis of Electromagnetic Fields Due to ESD in Slab Conductors
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper a mixed analytical-numerical approach that allows the determination of the current density distribution generated by passage of ESD current through an equipment metal structure is presented. A frequency domain analysis is used to obtain the current distribution and the analytical expression approximating the solution is determined in some situations.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Compatibility of Systems for Train Movement Control on Electrified Railways
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: On railways train location is determined automatically by systems controlling the condition of railway track (CRT). The CRT system consists of a transmitter and transducer receiving control signals, they are located on opposite ends of the line which is under control. The estimation of the track condition is carried out by the main device in a transducer. When the level of a control signal exceeds the threshold of the main device it is decided that the line is free and in good operating condition. Otherwise the line is considered to be occupied or out of order. On electrified lines rails are also used to conduct traction current, that is why the CRT transducers receive along with efficient signals parasitic signals at the input as well, the interference signals are produced by traction current. Greater power of electric trains (ET), application of thyristor method for regulation voltage in traction motors, a wide spread regime for recuperative braking intensify generation of interference signals. On the other hand the up-to-date instrumentation base of CRT equipment has the feature of insufficient efficiency of operating signals. These factors make the problem of electromagnetic compatibility of systems for controlling train movement and power supply on electrified railways urgent.

articleTitle: Research on Electromagnetic Compatibility in Automobile Industry
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the past decade the automobile industry introduced within its products the first electronic control systems. This implied the possibility of malfunctions due to the susceptibility of electronic systems to environmental electromagnetic fields. Problems related to the Electromagnetic Compatibility are very important today for the motor vehicle industry due to the growth of automotive electronics, the growth of environmental EM pollution, the increasing reliability requirements, the evolution of laws and regulations. EMC verifications on onboard systems are based on test procedures which have to comply with vehicle type approval, or "homologation", and product liability. The motor vehicle industry during the last years developed a set of laboratory bench test methodologies (i.e. Bulk Current Injection, Strip Line, TEM Cell) to be used as a support to the electronic product development in order to foresee possible criticities due to inadequate levels of electromagnetic immunity or emission. Tests performed on many electronic systems, however, showed only a certain degree of correlation between laboratory (at component level) and anechoic chamber (at vehicle level) test results. The laboratory techniques therefore, at today's state of the art, are considered as an useful and cost effective development tool, rather than a true alternative to the anechoic room testing. Computer simulations, based on mathematical models of electronic circuits, interconnections and bodywork, will be the basic tools to face the EMC problems scientifically, that means considering and analysing any variable and parameter. Being the simulation tools not available at short term, in the meantime EMC must be insured by means of a system design approach: this approach requires the capability to extract optimal subsystem-and component-level design and test specifications from the vehicle-level EMC specifications.

articleTitle: Transient Analysis of Planar Wire-Mesh Shields Loaded by Biisotropic Slabs
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Gratings made of thin wires are much used in applications of electromagnetic shielding. Unfortunately, the computation of the shielding effectiveness of a structure containing a grating is not simple, also from a numerical point of view, because of the complexity of the boundary conditions.

articleTitle: Low Frequency Shipborne Electromagnetic Design by Numerical Technique: Comparison of Computer Modelling Results with Measurements
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The problem of the analysis and simulation of installed antennas, when scatterer dimensions are smaller or comparable with respect to a wavelength, can be efficiently faced by means of frequency domain Method of Moments procedures. Tipically two kinds of MoM model basic geometries are considered, the first one based on wire elements only, and the second one based on interconnected wire and patch elements. Techniques based on both only wire and wire/patch geometries have been implemented in the numerical computation system of the Italian Navy. The performances of these techniques have been examined in the specific field of naval applications, by comparing wire-grid, wire-patch numerical simulation and measured results.

articleTitle: Shielding System for Power and Signal Processing Cable Transit
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In many different applications there are single apparatuses and control rooms with sophisticated electric or electronic equipment that are very sensitive to external disturbances. It is possible, for limiting these problems, to shield the room where there are sensible apparatuses. In any case, however power or signal cables must pass through the shielded wall and the shield efficiency is compromised. A system is described for suppression of disturbances that guarantees the shield continuity where there are holes for penetrating cables and pipes. Contact impedance and attenuation radiated interferences tests have been conducted in many different executive conditions.

articleTitle: The European Standardization in the EMC Field
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper presents the development of EMC standardization at European level in the EMC field. The strategy of CENELEC TCI 10 is explained especially in relation with a structure of different categories of standards : basic, generic and product (family) EMC standards. For each category, the latest developments are emphasized.

articleTitle: EMC Characterisation of Railway Networks Common Tests FS - DB - SNCF
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Italian State Railways accepted to take part in the Programme of Electromagnetic Compatibility Measurements promoted by Working Group WG4, which is part of Technical Committee TC9X of CENELEC (railway environment).

articleTitle: Traceability and Accuracy Aspects in EMC Compliance Testing
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A systematic approach to traceability and accuracy aspects in EMC compliance testing is given on the basis of standardized EMC terms with allowance for the probabilistic nature of EMI problems. Examples are given of the test ingredients which automatically follow from this approach. It is indicated how the traceability of (Basic) EMC Tests can be improved.

articleTitle: Theoretical and Experimental Evaluation of Radio Frequency Emission from Medium Power Inverters
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: a brief presentation on experiences made in the development of medium power inverters, from the EMC point of view. A practical problem is investigated, where the control of interferences represented a difficult problem, especially due to advanced phase of the project.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Electromagnetic Environment Around a Structure During a Lightning Stroke
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: It is introduced a discretization technique in the space and time of the phenomenon based on transmission line and wave propagation model to calculate the current distribution in a structure and on the infinitesimal time-varing dipole and image method to calculate the magnetic field around it.

articleTitle: A Matching Unit for 1 Metre Monopole Antennas for Land Vehicle EMC Measurements
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Subcommittee D of the CISPR is developing EMC standards to protect receivers used on-board vehicles from radio disturbances. One of these documents, which originated in C1SPR/D/WG2 is now in draft proposal form as a draft international standard (DIS) CISPR Publication 25-March 1994 [1]. In the long wave, medium wave, and short wave frequency bands, a matching unit to match a 1-m monopole antenna to a 50-Ω measuring system is required. Such a matching unit, the Electro-Mechanics Company (EMCO) Model 3301B, is described in this paper. The matching unit has a relatively flat frequency response from 9 kHz to 30 MHz, and can operate properly at a frequency of 150 kHz on signal levels at its input from 6.4 μV to 0.35 V, rms, in a bandwidth of 9 kHz. Its dynamic range is 95 dB, or greater, over the frequency range from 150kHz to 30 MHz, without using its internal attenuator.

articleTitle: Immunity Tests on Analog Telephone Sets. Set-Up and Results Related to the International Normative Trend
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: International standards on electromagnetic compatibility prescribe tests of immunity to continuous RF (Radio Frequency) disturbances conducted on the cables of an apparatus and to radiated disturbances. The paper describes the two methods used to assess the immunity of analogue telephone set (t.s.) to these conducted and radiated disturbances. Then the results of a set of measurements done on several analogue telephones are presented and discussed relating to the today normative trends.

articleTitle: Energy Absorption in the Head of Humans Exposed to the Electromagnetic Field Irradiated from a Cellular Phone in a Partially Closed Environment
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The aim of this study is the evaluation of the SAR distribution in the head of humans exposed to the electromagnetic field irradiated from a cellular phone in a partially closed environment. The finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method has been used to calculate the SAR in an anatomically based model of the head using 30112 cubic cells of 5 mm of side. The environmental effects are simulated through a reflecting wall located at various distances and positions with respect to the phone antenna.

articleTitle: Problems in Assessing the Actual Influence Between Close Ground Systems
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In developed urban and industrial areas, grounds systems that are not metallically connected may often be found. They are thus significantly interdependent as they are located in each other's area of influence. This situation causes a series of problems in terms of electrical compatibility and personnel safety. Since the theoretical calculation can result too much approximate or too much expensive, testing of the interdependent behaviour of ground electrodes is mandatory. Unfortunately accurate measure is often unfeasible, owing to the additional difficulty to measure both the hazardous voltages of the ground system where test ground current flows and the hazardous voltages of influenced ground systems. This paper discusses an approach to the above testing which relies on single or multiple auxiliary electrodes placed at short distance from the grounding electrodes. Thanks to this approach, a conservative test can be made of both Touch Voltage and Ground Potential Difference.

articleTitle: A New Look on Permissible Industrial Interference Levels
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: We analysed some results of interference measurements made with the help of standard measuring instruments having quasi-peak detector and those obtained from power spectrum analyser. It was shown that commonly used standard measuring instruments "lower" some energetic properties of random signals as compared to periodic signals. The mutual relations between results received in both cases are given for a few typical periodic and random interference signals.

articleTitle: Electric and Magnetic Fields at Low Frequency Produced by Spanish High Voltage Overhead Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: REE’s experience in calculated and measured transmission line electromagnetic fields are presented. A computer program to calculate these fields is described. Sensitivity studies are shown. The results of the computer program are checked with measurements performed near several transmission lines at 400 and 220 kV. Methodology and equipment used in the field measurements are presented.

articleTitle: On Relations Between Practical Stability and Some EMC Problems
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The close relations between formal procedure of the practical stability and some EMC problem are found. It leads to the situation when comparison systems can be built with more physical meaning. The example is considered.

articleTitle: EMC Design of a High Speed Digital System for Asynchronous Transfer Mode-Cross Connect Applications
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The pre-layout analysis procedure for high speed digital system are presented. Problems that arose during the design phase are discussed. In addition considerations on emission and switching will be given.

articleTitle: Simulation of Crosstalk in Printed Circuit Boards by Use of FDTD Implemented on a Personal Computer
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The FDTD technique is a powerful tool to analyse and understand electromagnetic problems. A simplified model of the technique has been developed and proposed to the students of the Electromagnetic Compatibility course held at the University of Ancona. Each group of three or four students developes, analyses and discusses the problem of the coupling between two parallel lines in conjunction with the traditional theoretical and experimental parts of the course.

articleTitle: Circuit Theory of the TEM-t with Application to the Measurement of the Shielding Effectiveness of Thin, Conductive Materials
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The characterization of the shielding effectiveness of thin, conductive materials can be determined over a large frequency range in a non-destructive way by measuring the transmission loss in a TEM-t cell. An equivalent circuit is developed for the empty and loaded cell. The necessary assumptions for correct use are discussed. The general theory and subsequent simplifications for thin, conductive materials allow a correct extraction of the conductivity of the material from the measurement results, as illustrated in a few examples.

articleTitle: Appraisal of Electromagnetic Compatibility of Power Electronic Converters with Traffic Control System During Design of the Suburban Railway
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A problem of electromagnetic disturbances caused be electric traction vehicles on a designed suburban railway is presented in the paper. A method of modelling and simulation is applied to analysis of the whole system composed of a power utility system, DC traction substation, overhead catenary and a traction vehicle with power electronic equipment and a.c. motors. Vehicle's current harmonics and equivalent psophometric current in the overhead catenary for different conditions is calculated and compared with the permitted values for signalling circuits. Some recommendations for traction vehicle's design as well as for signalling circuits are enclosed.

articleTitle: RF Exposure in a Shortwave Transmitter Environment Including the Influence of Building Structure and Human Body
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: According to a Swiss government survey (1993), RF exposure in a shortwave environment might be a source of insomnia, reduced concentration, high blood pressure and a general anxiety. The study performed specialised measurements and numerical simulations of the electromagnetic environment near the shortwave transmitter 'Schwarzenburg’ including an investigation of the RF exposure inside buildings and bedrooms. In a further step the influence of the human body on field distribution and attenuation was calculated. This allowed certain measurement guidelines and precautions to be deduced. This paper gives an overview of the gathered RF exposure data concentrating mainly on the specialised measurement techniques and related problems. Medical aspects related to RF exposure are not directly considered in this paper.

articleTitle: A Simulation Tool for ESD System Level Analysis in Space Applications
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Among transient threats that could compromise the success of a satellite's mission, the most dangerous and common is electrostatic discharge (ESD). This phenomenon, due to differential voltages among different points of the satellite's surface, produces both radiate electromagnetic (e.m.) fields and current, characterized by a wide frequency band. The paper describes the architecture of a simulation tool able to help the designer in a preliminary phase and furthermore to reproduce a configuration as close as possible to the operative one. The developed simulation tool, as described in a previous paper [1], has already been validated on simple and canonical configurations. In order to obtain a deeper validation, on realistic configurations, a measurement activity specially devoted to the ESD problem, has been planned out and performed at the Centro Elettrotecnico Sperimentale Italiano (CESI). The main scope of this paper is to show and discuss the comparisons between simulation results and measured data together with some remarks relevant to the modelling of lest set-up and its parassitic parameters.

articleTitle: On the Influence of Elevated Strike Objects on the Lightning Return Stroke Current and The Distant Electric Field
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Recent measurements of return stroke currents on instrumented towers reveal the existence of reflections at the tower bottom and top. In this paper, the effects of the reflections on both measured currents and the originated lightning electromagnetic fields are discussed. To this purpose, an extension of the Modified Transmission Line (MTL) return stroke model is given. The model takes into account multiple reflections at the bottom and at the top of the object and allows for the ‘decontamination’ of measured lightning currents from reflections due to the presence of the strike object. Our results show that even though the reflections might not be discernible in experimental recordings for tower heights as those used in Berger's and Garbagnati and Lo Piparo's investigations, the peak current might be significantly affected. Therefore, consideration of the reflections in the elaboration of meaningful statistics on lightning current is required, as well as an accurate evaluation of the tower reflection coefficients. Radiated fields calculated considering and neglecting the presence of the strike object differ. However it is shown that relatively short strike objects, such as triggered lightning launching structures, do not appreciably affect the calculated field peak values and overall wave shapes, but only the field derivatives.

articleTitle: The Prediction of Radiated Immunity Problems in Digital Systems
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The coupling of radio frequency energy from a source of interference to a digital system via an interconnecting cable is described. The subsequent low level interaction of the threat energy with the digital system is explored using theoretical and numerical techniques. Verification of the analysis by measurement is presented. The techniques have application in ensuring the Electromagnetic Compatibility of equipment at the design stage.

articleTitle: Topology of Broadband Integrated Circuit Interconnects
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In recent years the demand on the processing speed and hence higher clock frequencies nessecitated the use of compact planar integrated circuit technology on the same multilayer substrate such as that employed in Multi Chip Modules (MCM). In such circuits low cost and weight, increased frequency bandwidth, reduced parasitics and the ability to integrate passive and active circuits with minimum dispersions and reflections in the inteconnects are the crucial issues. In contrast to conventional VLSI design where lumped circuit analysis would suffice such broadband circuits require the distributed circuit concept in their design because the wavelength of the operating frequencies is comparable to the physical size of the circuit components used.

articleTitle: Instrument for the Measurement of High Frequency Current Distribution in Plate Conductors
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper reports the description of a new transducer suitable for the analysis of high frequency current distribution in plate conductors that is based on a novel design of the classic Rogowski coil. The experimental results from the calibration test are reported and noted, also with respect to other measuring methods.

articleTitle: The Spurious Transient Radiation of Antenna Array
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this work the linear vibrator array (LA) excited with non-stationary broad band and stationary monochrome signals is examined in rigorous electrodynamic task. Electromagnetic transients of LA are analyzed. The spurious, out-of-band, secondary EM fields are determined, which are very dangerous for radio electronic systems. The method of decision, main results of numerical calculations and recommendations on depressing of out-of-band radiation are presented.

articleTitle: ULF Electric Field Pulsations: Theoretical Analysis of Possible Origins
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The theoretical model has been proposed which confirmes that the nature of electric field pulsations can be explained, taking into account turbulent mixing of charged particles and thermal convection in the surface layer. The contribution of perturbations with the scales r ≳ L<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> into the structural function of electric field is estimated. For small-scale fluctuations (within the inertial interval) the exact expressions for the structural function and spectrum are obtained on the base of the set of ion balance and Poisson equations. It is shown that statistical characteristics (spectra, correlation and structural functions) of small scale fluctuations depend on the mechanisms of charge separation and transformation of neutral gas energy to the energy of electric field pulsations. Two mechanisms connected with neutral gas temperature and velocity fluctuations, are considered. Estimations, based on the theory proposed agree with the presented experimental results.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Compatibility of Communication Channels for Measuring Abyssal Parameters During the Process of Oil Well Drilling
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the several areas of the national economics it is very necessary to solve the questions of the field calculations particularly in order to determine the current distribution laws and the potential along the stretched metallic construction possessed its own longitudinal resistance and situated in the conducting medium. The solving of the similar questions is also required for the calculations of the potential distribution along the metallic construction in order to protect them electrochemically from corrosion, for using the electric channel of communication in order to measure the abyssal parameters during the oil wells' drilling, in the case of the underground and underwater pipelines and the conducting telemechanical communication Unes in the presence of the great current leakages (mist, raining etc.). The calculations of the electric communication channel are the most common and complex of all these cases because here the system exciting the electromagnetic field consists of the different sectors and each of these sectors has its certain influence on the current and potential distribution.

articleTitle: Conducted E.M Disturbances on the Telecommunication Terminal Equipment Ports
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This papér presents the statistical results of the called CELSUIS project launched by France Telecom in September 1992. Nine customer premises are selected in France and equiped with four channel transient recorders, in order to measure the overvoltages on the telecom and the mains ports, with a frequency bandwith up 2 Mhz.

articleTitle: A Hybrid MM-GTD Technique for the Analysis of Antennas Mounted on Arbitrary Bodies Modeled by Nurbs Surfaces
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The electromagnetic characterization of antennas attached to 3D-arbitrary shaped conducting bodies using the Moment Method [1] (MM) is significantly limited by computer storage of the matrix coupling. This paper examines a hybrid technique which combines the MM and GTD approximations. This MM-GTD scheme provides a way of extending the usefulness of the MM when moderate large bodies are considered. The antenna is defined like a numerical model formed by a set of electric and/or magnetic dipoles [2]. The bodies are modeled by means a collection of NURBS (Non Uniform Rational B-Splines) surfaces [3]. The developed method is efficient and versatile because it uses powerful geometrical modelling tools.

articleTitle: A Short Overview of the UK Master Degree in EMC
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper gives a brief overview of the UK M.Sc in EMC run by the universities of York and Hull.

articleTitle: Analysis of Near-Field Exposure and Radiation Characteristics of a Personal Communication Handset
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper deals with the influence that the presence of a person has on the performance of antennas for hand-held portable telephones. It is shown how the radiative characteristics of the system (far-field radiation pattern, magnitude of the near-field, electric and magnetic energy densities) are affected by the presence of the human body.

articleTitle: Design and Synthesis of Test Fixtures for Ferrite Based EMC Absorbers
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper describes design guidelines and methods for the synthesis of a coaxial test fixture for reflectivity measurement of ferrite tiles and multilayered ferrite based hybrid absorbers for EMC chamber applications. The test fixture was used to validate predicted values of reflectivity for prototype and production absorbers. The paper includes results of a survey of commercially available ferrite absorbers. Reflection properties of complex and simple absorber structures are characterized from 30-2000 MHz. Test results from the coaxial fixture are compared with other types of test fixtures as well as with calculated values.

articleTitle: EMC - a Must in Development of Automotive Electronics
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: EMC is very important in modern automotive electronics. Derived from physical aspects and demands of the practice a development strategy is given. Besides the applicating a lot of design rules testing is essential to reach the goal: EMC. The correlation problem between test results in bench tests and vehicle tests is reviewed. The responsibility for EMC depends on the system configuration. If parts of different suppliers are combined, the vehicle manufacturer has the responsibility on his own and has to specify parameters of the interfaces of the different components. Failures and malfunctions have to be defined depending on whether they are apparent for the driver in normal or abnormal operation of the vehicle. For the different test philosophies the pros and cons are discussed. The recommendation for the release procedure under technical and economic aspects is to apply strict limits for the vehicle testing in the production vehicle and performing bench tests as development tools.

articleTitle: The Need for Macro-Models in the Simulation of EMI Effects in Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper briefly reviews the previous work on the simulation of EMI effects in integrated circuits. Both component level and macro-models are considered. The relative merits of component level models and macro-models for EMI effects are discussed. In particular the problem of obtaining accurate data for component level models and the possibility of obtaining macro-model parameters by measurement are considered. The need to consider the coupling between all terminals is discussed. This contrasts with previous published work where only input to output effects are presented. Results are presented for some simple CMOS amplifier circuits.

articleTitle: Report on the Activities of CIGRÉ Study Committee 36 on Power System Electromagnetic Compatibility
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Issues of electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) related to large high-voltage electric power systems are dealt with by CIGRÉ (International Conference on Large High Voltage Electric Systems), through the activities of its Study Committee (SC) 36. A wide range of issues, including induction and interference effects, from power frequencies to radio and television frequencies, produced by transmission lines and substations, EMC within power plants and substations, voltage quality and possible health effects caused by power-frequency electric and magnetic fields (EMF), are addressed by SC 36. A brief account is given in this paper of the various studies presently being carried out by this committee.

articleTitle: Prediction Model Based on a Circuit-Concept Approach to the Radiation from a Bent Line on a Printed Circuit Board
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Radiation from a bent-trace on a printed circuit board is studied on a basis of circuit theory. Radiation from a transmission line is considered as in the reciprocal relationship with coupling of external fields to transmission line. Since a solution to the line equation for coupling is obtained in terms of analytical functions, radiation is also expressed in quite the similar form to coupling. Under the TEM approximation, the prediction algorithm for bent lines is discussed on the theoretical and the experimental viewpoints.

articleTitle: The Progress of the International EMC Standardization for the Control Systems in Electrical Power Installations
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper presents the progress of the EMC standardization at international level for the apparatus intended for use by Electricity Utilities. The particular needs of the installations related to the production, transport and distribution of electricity are pointed out, and information on the UNIPEDE initiative of preparing EMC specifications dedicated to Electricity Utilities is given. In the following, the problems of coordinated EMC specifications for the different apparatus of interest of the Electricity Utilities are pointed out. A general overview on the document in preparation is given, with some considerations on possible advantages to have the unification of the requirements.

articleTitle: Uncertainty and Traceability of Antenna Calibration
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The two most common methods of antenna calibration are the reference antenna and standard site methods. For the reference antenna method, the Motor Industry Research Association (MIRA) have had two sets of resonant dipoles antennas accurately calibrated by the National Physical Laboratory (NPL) in the UK to be the transfer standard to obtain traceability. It is shown that very little additional uncertainty is added to the uncertainty in the antenna factors values given by a national standards laboratory so long as good measurement practice is adhered to. For the standard site method, a procedure for finding site imperfections using reference antennas and a method of combining this quantity into the total uncertainty of antenna calibration are described. An uncertainty of better than ± 1.5 dB is achievable using this method on the MIRA Open Area Test Site (OATS).

articleTitle: Some Educational Actions on EMC Under the European Programs of Erasmus, Commett and Tempus
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper, an overview will be given of some educational actions on EMC, which are funded by the European Union (formerly EEC).

articleTitle: Methods for Analysing Electromagnetic Compatibility Between Cellular Mobile Communication Systems Deployed Along Highways and Radio Communication Stations of Other Services
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: At present cellular mobile communication systems (CMS) have gained wide acceptance. In Europe two CMS standards are most widely spread: NMT-450 and GSM. The former operates in the range of 450 MHz, the latter at 900 MHz [1].

articleTitle: Earthing and Bonding in SIP's Central Offices
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper presents a summary of the researches carried out by SIP inside a small central office in order to test the new earthing and bonding configuration recommended by the most important International Organization. The most important results obtained are presented. The paper describes also the earthing and bonding configuration (Mesh-BN) that SIP is considering to use for its new central offices. It is also presented the methodology followed by SIP to find the existing central offices which could need a redesign of the existing earthing and bonding configuration (STAR) to improve their EMC performances.

articleTitle: Ground Return Overhead Lines Parameters
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper presents Carson’s formulae, for the contribution of the earth to the transmission line parameters, in a modified form, which is closer to the physical nature of the problem. Also, are proposed approximate formulae for the contribution of the earth, valid in specified conditions. Diagrams are given which enable a quick computation.

articleTitle: Analysis of Radiated Emissions in PCBs Using Integral Equations Technique
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: An integral equation technique solved by the method of moment is proposed to characterize printed circuit boards (PCB) as sources of radiated emissions. The current distributions are computed either for circuits having or without a ground plane. The radiated field is calculated from the obtained current distributions which are modelled as an array of elementary dipoles. The theoretical results of the radiated field are compared with measurements where a good agreement is observed. Finally, some simulations for several geometrical and electrical parameters corresponding to the basic elementary circuit used in practice are presented in order to show what are the less radiated Configurations.

articleTitle: A Model to Investigate Lightning Performances and Coupling Effects Among Buried Long Electrodes
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper a field approach to investigate the transient performance of long grounding electrodes is presented. The method is based on the spectral analysis and, as a great advantage in comparison with circuit approach, it enables us to calculate electrical and magnetic fields in the surrounding soil. As a particular matter, this paper, after having investigated the behaviour of a single electrode, is devoted to study fields transferred from an electrode to a separate one, in any mutual position. As examples, time behaviour of main electric quantities are reported assuming a lightning stroke injected current.

articleTitle: The IEE Distance Learning Video Package on EMC
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper describes the production method and philosophy of the IEE Distance Learning video package on EMC.

articleTitle: An Integrated Educational Software Package for the Analysis of Crosstalk on PCB's
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper, the realisation of an integrated package is discussed for the analysis of crosstalk on PCB’s. It is based on the use of different existing packages, which are combined into on easy to use integrated one. The analysis starts from the geometrical configuration of two or three adjacent tracks on a PCB. The program creates automatically an input-file for Pspice simulation, based on the method of decoupled modes. The main advantage of this package is that all available component libraries within Pspice can be used.

articleTitle: High Linear Amplifier with Special Negative Feedback
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A simple and efficient technique to reduce the nonlinear behavior of amplifiers is presented. This technique is based on the introduction of a special type of negative linear feedback to a main amplifier. By using Volterra series and the structural theory of systems, it has been demonstrated that the presented technique only compensates the nonlinearities without reducing the linear gain of the main amplifier as it is the case when the conventional feedback technique is used.

articleTitle: EM Compatibility Between GSO/FSS and LEO/MSS Feeder Links
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Mobile Satellite Services (MSSs) represent one of the fastest growing segment of the satellite industry. Besides the existing satellite networks in geostationary satellite orbit (GSO), that currently provide voice and data communications for a variety of land-, maritime- and aeronautical-based applications, new mobile satellite services are just around the corner. These new systems, employng multiple satellite constellations in low and medium earth orbits (LEOs, MEOs), are aiming to deliver a whole new level of service, i.e. a worldwide communications via handheld telephones. The entrants of these systems will make the spectral congestion a very serious problem on a world-wide basis. Since non-geostationary satellites will pass over all countries in their orbits, a global coordination will be required for these systems. Thus, in order to improve spectrum efficiency, new sharing criteria need to be developed. Assuming that future LEO/MSS feeder links would typically be provided in fixed satellite service (FSS) allocations, the aim of this paper is to investigate the nature of the potential interference between GSO and LEO satellite networks and propose possible means to facilitate on a shared basis the operations of both systems.

articleTitle: Modelling of Lightning-Induced Voltages on Overhead Lines: Recent Developments
publicationTitle: EMC'94 Roma, International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Return-stroke lightning models and coupling models developed recently permit a fairly good estimation of overvoltages induced by indirect lightning strokes. However, some discrepancies that still exist between measured data and calculations stress the necessity to incorporate leader effects into the models, to improve our understanding of ground conductivity effects on the formation of the fields, and to obtain more experimental data.
